Prompt.title: Prompt
Prompt.description: Represents a single AI prompt managed by the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Prompt entity.

title.description: The title or name of the prompt.

description.description: A detailed description explaining the purpose or context of the prompt.

content.description: The actual text content of the prompt.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the prompt was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the prompt was last updated.

definition.description: Stores individual AI prompts created and owned by a specific user. This collection is private to each user. Includes denormalized 'ownerId' field for authorization independence, which matches the '{userId}' path parameter.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this prompt.

params.name: promptId
params.description: The unique identifier of the prompt.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for managing user prompts follows a strict path-based ownership model to ensure robust security, scalability, and debuggability. Each user's prompts will be stored in a subcollection under their unique user ID:

`/users/{userId}/prompts/{promptId}`

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
This structure inherently provides strong authorization independence. Each `Prompt` document will explicitly include an `ownerId` field. This `ownerId` will match the `userId` segment in the document's path. By denormalizing the `ownerId` directly into the `Prompt` document, security rules can evaluate access requests without needing to perform `get()` operations on a parent 'user' document. This eliminates hierarchical authorization dependencies, making security rules atomic, simpler, and less prone to issues during batched writes or transactions. For instance, a rule can simply check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId` and `request.auth.uid == userId` (from the path wildcard) without external lookups.

**QAPs (Secure List Operations):**
The structural segregation of prompts under `/users/{userId}/prompts` directly supports Query-As-Permissions (QAPs). When a user requests their list of prompts, the query will be implicitly scoped to their specific `userId` path (e.g., `/users/ABCDEF/prompts`). Firestore security rules will then enforce that `request.auth.uid` must match the `{userId}` wildcard in the path for any `list` or `read` operation. This design ensures that users can only query and retrieve *their own* prompts, preventing unauthorized access to other users' data without requiring complex, potentially insecure, filtering logic within the security rules themselves. The data is pre-filtered by its location.

**Other Principles:**
*   **Clarity of Intent:** The path `/users/{userId}/prompts/{promptId}` clearly indicates that each prompt belongs to a specific user. The `ownerId` field within the document further solidifies this intent.
*   **DBAC:** Authorization relies solely on `request.auth.uid` matching the `userId` path parameter and the `ownerId` field within the document. No custom claims or separate role documents are needed for this private user data.
*   **Structural Segregation:** All documents within the `/users/{userId}/prompts` collection have the same security posture (owner-only access), simplifying rule sets.
*   **Invariants:** Ownership (`ownerId`) and timestamps (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`) are maintained within each `Prompt` document.
